product.title: Teenage Engineering EP-133 K.O. II Extended Player - EP–40 riddim
product.description: A portable sampler sequencer and composer with advanced fluid sequencing, stereo sound, and hands-free sampling for creative music production.

dossier.headline: EP–40 Riddim Sampler Composer
dossier.summary: The EP-133 K.O. II Extended Player – EP–40 riddim is a portable sampler, sequencer and composer from Swedish design company Teenage Engineering. Described as a complete rhythm and bass system inspired by reggae, dub, dancehall and sound system culture, it runs on four AAA batteries or USB-C.

facts.label: Founders
facts.value: Jesper Kouthoofd, David Eriksson, Jens Rudberg, David Möllerstedt

facts.label: Series
facts.value: EP series (EP-133 K.O. II / EP–40 riddim)

story.title: A Swedish design house
story.detail: Teenage Engineering is a consumer electronics and design company founded in 2005 in Stockholm by Jesper Kouthoofd, David Eriksson, Jens Rudberg and David Möllerstedt.

story.title: Rooted in sound system culture
story.detail: The EP–40 riddim is positioned as a complete rhythm and bass system, a sampler, sequencer and composer inspired by reggae, dub, dancehall and sound system culture.

story.title: Part of the EP family
story.detail: The EP–40 riddim is a variant within the same EP series as the standard EP-133 K.O. II Extended Player, described as a powerful sampler, sequencer and composer.

references.title: EP-133 K.O. II
references.detail: The standard EP-133 K.O. II Extended Player shares the same product family and form factor as the EP–40 riddim.

references.title: MoMA Design Store listing
references.detail: Retailed through the MoMA Design Store, which describes it as a powerful sampler, sequencer and composer.
